tummyTuck.title: Tummy Tuck
tummyTuck.excerpt: A specialized procedure to remove excess skin and tighten the abdominal area for a more balanced shape, with a tailored plan and close pre/post-operative follow-up.
tummyTuck.details:
Remove excess skin and fat
Tighten abdominal muscles and improve contour
Clear, long-lasting results
Performed under specialist medical supervision
A tailored plan and full follow-up before and after the procedure

gastricBypass.title: Gastric Bypass
gastricBypass.excerpt: One of the most effective bariatric surgeries for sustained weight loss and improving obesity-related conditions such as diabetes and hypertension, with long-term nutritional follow-up.
gastricBypass.details:
Creates a smaller stomach pouch to help you feel full faster
Reroutes part of the intestine to reduce calorie absorption
Candidates: BMI 40+ or BMI 35+ with comorbidities
Benefits: significant sustained weight loss, improved diabetes control
Requires vitamins/minerals supplementation and long-term dietary commitment

hiatalHernia.title: Hiatal Hernia Repair (Laparoscopic)
hiatalHernia.excerpt: Minimally invasive repair to relieve reflux symptoms and restore quality of life, with less pain and a faster recovery back to daily activities.
hiatalHernia.details:
Laparoscopic (no traditional open surgery)
Less pain after surgery
Faster recovery and return to daily life
Effective relief for reflux/heartburn
Durable long-term results
Repositions the stomach and repairs the diaphragm opening precisely

q1.a: It reduces stomach size and reroutes part of the intestine to support weight loss and improve diabetes control.

q2.a: Yes. It’s commonly performed laparoscopically with smaller incisions, less pain, and faster recovery.

q3.q: Who are candidates for bariatric surgery?
q3.a: Typically BMI 40+ or BMI 35+ with comorbidities such as diabetes or hypertension.

q4.q: When can I return to normal life after laparoscopic surgery?
q4.a: Recovery is usually faster, but the timeline depends on your case and the procedure type.
